summary.headline: Aarti Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR 2,422 crore and EBITDA 29% to INR 342 crore, with FY27 capex guided at INR 700-800 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 2,422 crore (up 9% YoY), EBITDA INR 342 crore (up 29%) and PAT INR 137 crore (up 43%), helped by volume growth and higher utilisation. West Asia disruption raised benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene and methanol prices by over 60%, lifted freight costs and cut Middle East shipments, which are about 9-10% of revenue. Zone IV projects are delayed 3-4 months on contract labour shortages, with the bulk now expected in FY27. Management guided FY27 capex to INR 700-800 crore and aims to reduce net debt in FY27 despite working-capital pressure.

segments.name: Energy applications
segments.commentary: About 40% of revenue; volumes down 4% QoQ on lower Middle East exports. Expansion to 360 KTPA is on track and expected to commission soon. Middle East is about 9-10% of company revenue, mostly energy.

segments.name: Agrochemicals
segments.commentary: Steady volume growth but margin pressure continues. A new $150 million multiyear agro intermediate contract runs to March 2030 with no incremental capex.

segments.name: Polymers
segments.commentary: Strong growth phase on EV-linked demand; MPDA continues to underperform due to Chinese competition.

segments.name: Dyes, pigments and paints
segments.commentary: Share of revenue about 10-11%. Demand pressure in 3,3'-DCBH globally, partly offset by domestic demand; some low-margin demand destruction possible in 3-6 months.

segments.name: Pharma
segments.commentary: Stable in the quarter; PNCB chain expected to benefit from China anti-involution from Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guided at INR 700-800 crore (about INR 150 crore a year is maintenance), funding Zone IV completion and a new INR 200-250 crore backward-integration contract.
Zone IV: calcium chloride and multipurpose plant to be commercialised within the quarter; remaining blocks commissioned through FY27 after a 3-4 month delay; initial revenue from Q2 FY27.
Management aims to reduce net debt in FY27 despite higher working capital, as capex intensity falls and cash flow improves.
Tax rate guided at about 9-15% going forward.
Working capital target of 55-60 days, with the company currently above this level.
Augene (Superform JV) to commission around June-July 2026; recycling JV to commission in CY26.
Interest-cost and EBITDA potential from Zone IV and the UPL JV unchanged at INR 300-450 crore, but realisation may slip 6-7 months.
capex_capacity: Zone IV total capex about INR 1,800-2,000 crore; gross block expected at INR 9,500-10,000 crore by end FY27.
Energy expansion to 360 KTPA on track for commissioning soon.
Contract labour availability in the capex region down 35%, delaying last-mile pipeline work.
Augene JV and recycling JV commissioning in 2026; DCB debottlenecking under way.
About 50% of the Bayer/Dicamba-linked asset is used for one intermediate, with steady volumes.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices (benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene, methanol) rose over 60% in the quarter; some more than doubled.
Agro pricing is up sharply from January, but the company is holding spreads rather than absolute prices; full pass-through expected over 3-6 months.
NCB margins and pricing improved on China's anti-involution policy; DCB remains robust on EV demand.
MMA economics are volatile with gasoline-naphtha cracks ranging from negative to up $20/bbl; Middle East shipments physically halted, US shipments steady, Europe starting.
Physical supply of methanol (about a couple of months' cover) and sulfur (a few weeks' cover) is secure.

qa_highlights.question: Was there an inventory gain in Q4 margins, especially in March?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory impact was not significant; FX gain was about INR 10 crore in the quarter, and raw material costs also rose in March.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: About 9-10% of revenue on an annual average basis, mostly energy; product is being redirected elsewhere, with the full impact visible in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY27 capex fall and what is the breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was INR 1,125 crore as guided, not reduced; FY27 guided at INR 700-800 crore mainly for Zone IV, the new long-term contract and about INR 150 crore maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is debt high despite about INR 600 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash was a late-March term loan disbursement; net debt is about INR 4,300 crore, with bulk of cash used to repay debt in early April. Working capital rose INR 250-300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 freight and other-expense jump and inventory build?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight rates rose from mid-February, exports were 57% of revenue, and US mix lengthened voyages; INR 409 crore stock build reflects goods in transit not yet recognised as revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Are Zone IV EBITDA and the net debt/EBITDA target at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost and operating-leverage initiatives are on track; the EBITDA potential is unchanged but may slip 6-7 months. Net debt/EBITDA was about 3.6x at year-end.

risks_watch: Middle East flows halted for 6-8 weeks; full Q1 FY27 impact on energy volumes depends on West Asia stabilisation.
Working capital and net debt rise if crude moves to USD 140-150/bbl.
Zone IV labour shortage and 3-4 month delay; check commissioning and first revenue in Q2 FY27.
Potential demand destruction in low-margin dyes and pigments over 3-6 months.
Unhedged USD 87 million FX loan; further rupee depreciation would add revaluation losses.
MPDA and agro margins remain under pressure from Chinese competition.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic: management stresses resilience and volume gains but repeatedly flags near-term West Asia risk, labour delays and working-capital strain. It was evasive on Zone IV revenue, asset-level capex and MMA demand split, citing pricing volatility.
key_quotes: The overall demand environment for our basket of products remained largely stable.
Our capex for FY27 is expected to be in the range of INR 700 crore to INR800 crore as we continue our journey to optimize capex and maximize the returns.
I think it is not easy to handle more than 60% increase in raw material pricing in a 2 weeks' time frame.

financial_highlights.change: on USD 87 million unhedged loan; rupee moved about INR 5 to 94.8

adds.what: Zone IV multipurpose plant and calcium chloride plant (commercialisation within quarter), remaining 5 chemistry blocks commissioned through FY27

growth.why: FY27 capex guided at INR 700-800 crore (cut vs FY26's INR 1,125 crore) with Zone IV blocks and 360 KTPA energy expansion backing volume growth, though Zone IV is delayed 3-4 months and no FY27 revenue growth % was given; Q4 revenue +9% and EBITDA +29% YoY.
